page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The virtual machine executes on dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors built on x86_64 architecture across 8 physical cores with two hardware threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 2.0 GB per thread, complemented by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is enabled via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, accompanied by base AVX support, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

Benchmark measurements indicate balanced compute and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a top-quartile stress-ng single-core result of 2,926.98 alongside an average multi-core score of 23,457.88. Memory benchmarks demonstrate solid throughput, registering a PassMark memory score in the upper 25% and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 80.47 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 17.72 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads, 16.81 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 301.82 tokens per second for small language model text generation.

The c2d-highcpu-16 includes zero local storage and no dedicated GPU accelerators, necessitating reliance on networked storage volumes for disk operations. By focusing budget allocations strictly on dedicated execution cores rather than expansive memory capacity or bundled NVMe drives, this instance maximizes compute density per resource unit. It functions efficiently for compute-bound tasks such as parallel compilation, CI/CD runners, batch processing, media transcoding, and distributed web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized instance providing 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Featuring an x86_64 configuration across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it maintains a lean 1:2 memory-to-core allocation of 2.0 GB per thread alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Synthetic tests indicate strong single-core compute performance and upper-quartile memory benchmarks, complementing solid multi-core execution in software compilation and web serving throughput. The instance provisions no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, directing hardware allocation purely toward CPU density. This architectural profile makes the c2d-highcpu-16 well configured for CPU-bound production environments, including continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, distributed web serving, and lightweight model inference.
